observations.finding: The primary coordinates are predicted endpoint world-frame forecasts in A, not current physical atom positions or velocity. The complete supplied window has 50 observed nodes, t=0.00 through 0.49, within the learning window [0.0,0.5]. Regional means equally average children within extant parent and score stratum, then batches; independent survival support is 14 batches. Terminal score time is 0.99 and terminal state time is 1.0, so endpoint forecasts, local selection strata, terminal survival and final quality have distinct meanings.

Whole-window high-minus-low endpoint contrasts favor smaller x/y shape moments and larger short-scale pair kernels: shape_xx -0.495 z (CI -0.648 to -0.320, q=0.000813; 13/14 batches negative), shape_yy -0.513 (CI -0.620 to -0.424, q=0.0000149; 14/14 negative), and pair_kernel_2.5 +0.631 (CI +0.495 to +0.758, q=0.0000219; 14/14 positive). Pair kernels 1.5/3.5 are also positive in all batches, 5.0 in 12/14, while 7.0 is negative in all 14. Corresponding integrated score correlations are modest, about -0.195 to +0.213; these are selection associations.

Landmark contrasts differ by region. Landmark_00 has lower softmin (-0.481 z, q=0.000813, all batches negative) and higher occupancy3 (+0.545 z, q=0.000235, all batches positive). Landmarks 02/06/18 instead have positive integrated softmin (+0.253/+0.294/+0.264 z) and negative occupancy5 (-0.323/-0.365/-0.311 z), all with q<0.006 and at least 12/14 batches agreeing. A universal direction toward every landmark is unsupported.

Parent-debiased local moments reproduce lower x/y covariance in examples such as landmark_00 local_cxx -0.579 z (q=0.00184) and local_cyy -0.575 (q=0.000131), landmark_07 local_cyy -0.646 (q=0.0000708), and landmark_16 local_cyy -0.672 (q=0.000131); their batch agreement is 13/14 or 14/14. Local y offsets are spatially heterogeneous: landmark_02/06/18 effects are +0.405/+0.425/+0.425 z with all batches positive, while landmark_12 is -0.529 z with all batches negative. Gaussian regions overlap, so these are coordinate patterns without a unique residue mechanism.

Across all 600 regional tests, the reported q values support 69/200 level contrasts, 22/200 enrichment-change-rate contrasts and 21/200 parent-edge contrast rates at q<0.05. Examples include increasing landmark_01 local_dz enrichment rate (+1.621 standardized rate, CI +1.097 to +2.185, q=0.00196, all batches positive), declining landmark_04 local_dy (-2.347, q=0.00495, 12/14 negative), and negative landmark_04 local_cxx parent-edge contrast rate (-4.596, q=0.00325, all batches negative). These compare supplied forecast moments or parent edges; they do not measure physical atom velocity.

Empirical node contrasts change substantially across the full observed window. Landmark_00 local_cxx starts at -0.060 z, reaches -1.636 at t=0.24 and ends at -0.088; local_cyy starts at +0.126, reaches -1.336 at t=0.24 and ends at +0.253. Landmark_06 local_dy starts at +0.326, reaches +1.270 at t=0.20 and ends at -0.334. Strong integrated contrasts can therefore weaken or reverse by the last node; supplied node functions describe their score-conditioned populations rather than individual trajectories.

Only 1/74 increment contrasts has reported q<0.05: landmark_00_softmin success-minus-failure integrated rate -4.914 standardized rate (CI -6.855 to -2.616, q=0.0461, 13/14 batches negative). Occupancy3 at the same landmark is +4.277 but q=0.0811, and shape_xx/yy rates have q=0.0951/0.1606. The broad endpoint level pattern is much more supported than a general increment-direction hypothesis.

All 24 selected global/landmark feature fits fail the supplied runtime fidelity audit: none is allowed for Legendre runtime use. Relative node RMSE ranges from 0.386 to 0.931 against an allowed maximum 0.35; strong sign conflicts range from 0 to 15 nodes, and quiet-node large-fit fractions range from 0.08 to 0.34. Integrated feature selection does not validate the fitted time direction.

No survival field or survival-change-rate test among 400 has BH q<0.05. The strongest reported q is 0.1204; landmark_00 soft_mass survival enrichment is +0.365 z (CI +0.200 to +0.515, 12/14 batches positive) but remains exploratory after correction. Lineage coverage is sparse: 349/700 batch-nodes have fewer than three ancestors, 531/700 fewer than six, teachers range from 17 to 28 per node, and there are at most two teachers per batch. Selection evidence cannot be promoted to validated terminal survival or terminal affinity effects.

Leave-one-batch-excluded sparse salient-field teacher selection loses geometric information relative to Hungarian fixed-frame RMS: excess fixed RMS is +0.0810 A (batch CI95 +0.0697 to +0.0921), with top-four teacher overlap 0.470 (CI95 0.427 to 0.515). This supports a representation-fidelity concern for compression, but not a causal affinity advantage for any reward. Chosen-teacher score correlations are observational: compressed 0.102 versus full 0.0641, and the audit excludes the full score-weighted reward and FLOWR Jacobian.

The incumbent program_20 has the highest supplied discovery mean_pic50_delta, +0.23030, with validity change +0.01 and MMFF relief per-heavy median/p90 0.47695/0.95455. Program_3 is almost tied in mean (+0.22929) but has p90 1.25258. Program_19 trades a slightly smaller mean gain (+0.21284) for p90 0.90787, and program_8 has the lowest p90 0.73102 but mean gain +0.13900. Program_4 has the highest best-valid pIC50 (8.55804) but validity change -0.02. These adaptive reused discovery results motivate prospective comparisons; they do not establish a statistically superior program.

hypotheses: Retain registered incumbent program_20 as the candidate for the paired generation comparison, with no scalar updates: endpoint_pointcloud, endpoint reference, native_rms_ratio=0.33, teacher_neighbors=4, teacher_endpoint_temperature_A2=4.0, teacher_score_beta=2.0, mixture_temperature=0.5 and time_ramp_power=0.0 over [0.0,0.5]. Test final predicted affinity, all-attempt validity/failures and physical mean/tail outcomes prospectively before adoption. Benefit to final affinity is unproven, and these untyped coordinate proxies identify neither chemical interactions nor energies. Do not turn the level association into an unconditional shrinking or attraction rule. counterevidence.finding: Whole-window significance is not a valid node-level sign schedule. At the last node landmark_06 softmin is empirically -0.402 z but fitted +0.294; shape_yy is empirically +0.163 but fitted -0.513. All 24 audited fits are disallowed for runtime use.

No terminal-survival test passes joint correction, despite some intervals excluding zero. Sparse ancestors and at most two teachers per batch limit precision; repeated descendants cannot increase the independent sample size.

Compression chooses teachers with greater geometric distance, but its reported chosen-teacher score correlation exceeds the full-distance value. Neither distance excess nor observational score correlations prove that an uncompressed reward improves affinity.

Retention of program_20 has competing discovery tradeoffs: program_19 and program_8 have lower relief p90, and program_4 has higher best-valid pIC50. Quality rows provide no comparison intervals or independent validation, so the incumbent is a candidate rather than a proven optimum.

Some occupancy3 differences are statistically significant but tiny in effect size: landmark_01 -0.00196 z, landmark_03 -0.00684, landmark_05 -0.00472. The supplied feature-selection rule excludes scale-floor fields and requires absolute integrated z>=0.1; significance alone does not justify a reward feature.

Endpoint geometry levels have stronger support than most increment-rate analogues: shape_xx, shape_yy and pair_kernel_2.5 rates have q=0.0951, 0.1606 and 0.2082. Landmark_00 softmin is the sole q<0.05 increment result and is close to that threshold.

limitations: Only the bound evidence was used. Raw trajectories, source implementations, unbound references and held-out inference results were not inspected; no generation comparison or source edit was performed.

Generation batches are independent units; within-batch nodes, score strata and repeated descendants are correlated. Regional moments use the stated parent debiasing, but the supplied summaries cannot support candidate-level independent replication.

The 50 observed nodes end at t=0.49. No supplied observation justifies interpolation as learned support, a result at t=0.50, extrapolation beyond the window, or replacing the required native continuation. Terminal score and state clocks differ.

Reported contrasts and rates use standardized scales; geometric information-audit distances are in A. The bound quality rows do not state physical units for MMFF relief per heavy atom, and no material-regression margin is supplied.

Selection preference, success/failure increment strata, terminal survival and final predicted pIC50 are different populations and labels. Missing future labels remain missing and cannot be counted as failed affinity; survival tests are not terminal-affinity tests.

Regional Gaussian supports overlap and contain no atom-type fields. Compact moment functions do not reconstruct full coordinates; untyped distances or covariance cannot identify contacts, residue mechanisms or interaction energies.

Discovery batches are adaptive and reused, with no independent validation, all-attempt sample counts, explicit failure accounting, physical mean comparison or paired uncertainty in the bound quality rows. The all-attempt objective and absence of material strain regression must be established in the prospective paired comparison.

The execution contract allows only bounded compiler-accepted scalar changes, exact learned nodes and FLOWR endpoint VJP, with no extra production forward call, affinity-head gradient, SMC or graph veto. The retained registered candidate requires no invented feature or new parameter direction.
